newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries open higher, seen in tight ranges.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries open higher, seen in tight ranges.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries opened a bit higher on Tuesday, boosted by another round of foreign buying and a report signalling week consumer spending last week.
But market participants expect Treasuries to stick to fairly narrow ranges in the absence of key economic data until Friday.
The 30-year bond was at 96-21/32, up 4/32 from Monday, while its yield edged down to 6.89 percent from 6.90 percent.
Aiding the market in early trading was a reported 0.5 percent drop in the BTM-Schroders in the week ended May 31. Players had anticipated a strong Memorial Day holiday report.
Meanwhile, players said the market has solid underlying support, evidenced by the recovery Monday afternoon, leading Treasuries higher for the third straight day.

"The market has a good tone. People are very comfortable buying the dip -- as long as the dollar remains firm," said Jim Stewart, senior trader at Yamaichi International (America) Inc. "The market has support, not just from dealers. We have seen real retail buying."
Much of the buying has come from overseas accounts, said traders, who saw scattered buying in two- to 10-year notes from central banks and Japanese life insurers the past few sessions.
Some have noted that other Far East countries, such as Singapore, China and Thailand, have been big buyers of Treasuries.

Meanwhile, concerns over European Monetary Union in the wake of the Socialists victory in France on Sunday, coupled with the ongoing dispute between the German government and the Bundesbank over gold revaluation, have prompted increased buying from Europe.
At the same time, U.S. accounts are slowly coming to grips with the idea the Federal Reserve may not raise interest rates next month, but rather in late summer.
Still, with the May employment report -- due on Friday -- in the wings, any further significant gains are seen limited.
One issue, though, that should garner interest is the 10-year note.

With numerous 10-year offerings this session including Toyota and the Asian Development Bank, players forsee significant swap interest in 10-year Treasuries -- and as a result, the issue is expected to be rich in the repo market.
Also this session, the market will eye a speech by San Francisco Fed president Robert Parry, who is slated to speak in Alaska at 1120 EDT/1520 GMT.
As for economic data, the Conference Board will release its April leading indicators report at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT, followed by the Johnson Redbook weekly retail sales report at 1455 EDT/1855 GMT.

In early morning trade, bill rates were flat to three basis points lower. The two-year note was unchanged at 100-2/32 to yield 6.22 percent. The five-year note was at 100, up 2/32 to yield 6.50 percent and 10-year notes were up 2/32 at 99-26/32 to yield 6.65 percent.
